narrative:
The model determined that you have a 63% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is well above the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the lack of any property you could offer as collateral, and the length of the loan you requested. 

Your checking account balance in the 0-200 DM range was the single biggest reason for the rejection. While nearly 60% of approved applicants have no checking account at all, this modest positive balance still signaled higher risk to the model and pushed the prediction toward denial. 

The fact that you have no property to pledge as security was the second most important factor and also increased your risk score substantially. Only about 8% of approved customers lack any registered property, so this absence worked against you.

Finally, the 36-month duration you requested was significantly longer than the 19-month average among approved loans. This longer commitment added further weight toward a bad-credit prediction.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed several positive aspects of your profile, such as your steady job and clean credit history.

To improve your chances on a future application, consider applying for a shorter-term loan, building up your savings, or waiting until you have acquired some form of property that can serve as collateral. These steps would directly address the main concerns that led to the current denial.
